newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Tuesday.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March consumer price index and business inventories data.
The consumer price index for March is forecast to show a gain of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.3 percent increase reported in February.
March business inventories are expected to show an increase of 0.2 percent against February's 0.1 percent gain.
"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.
"All eyes are on tonight's release of the CPI and retail sales figures, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact here," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday and Wednesday/Thursday rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent and four-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16.
Nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent and twelve-months rose 1/8 point to 6-7/16 6-5/16 percent.
